The Udyog Bharari 2024 event was held on 29th September 2024 at the Ganesh Kala Krida Manch, Swargate, Pune, more than 2000 participants.
The program commenced with a welcome address by Shri. Shivaji Patil, Deputy CEO of MIDC, who highlighted MIDCs contributions to industrial development.
Several government scheme videos, including CMEGP, PM Vishwakarma, MAITRI, Mukhyamantri Majhi Ladki Bhahi, and Mukhyamantri Yuva Prashikshan Yojna, were presented to the audience.

Cheques for the CMEGP scheme were distributed to 10 participants by Hon. Uday Samant, along with six certificates for PM Vishwakarma participants. During his address, Hon. Uday Samant acknowledged the efforts of government officers, emphasized the support for women entrepreneurs under the CMEGP scheme, and discussed a defense investment of ₹10,000 crore in Maharashtra. He also urged industry officers and associations to support foundations like NAAM.

Hon. Shrirang Appa Chandu Bharne praised the governments efforts in industrial development and the success of schemes like CMEGP. Hon. Dr. Chandrakant Pulkundwar highlighted the role of various policies in fostering industrial growth. Hon. Anil Bhandari discussed the contributions of major companies like Tata, Mahindra, and TCS to the economy. The event concluded with a vote of thanks by Shri.Shailesh Rajput, Joint Director of Industries, Pune Region.

Indias Foreign Trade Policy (FTP) provides the basic framework of policy and strategy for promoting exports and trade. It is periodically reviewed to adapt to the changing domestic and international scenario.
The current Foreign Trade Policy (2015-20) focusses on improving Indias market share in existing markets and products as well as exploring new products and new markets.

Indias Foreign Trade Policy also envisages helping exporters leverage benefits of Goods and Service Tax (GST), closely monitoring export performances, improving ease of trading across borders, increasing realization from Indias agriculture-based exports and promoting exports from Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) and labour-intensive sectors.
Customs Duty refers to the tax imposed on the goods when they are transported across the international borders.

The objective behind levying customs duty is to safeguard each nations economy, jobs, environment, residents, etc., by regulating the movement of goods, especially prohibited and restrictive goods, in and out of any country.
Types of Custom Duty Basic Customs Duty (BCD) Countervailing Duty (CVD) Additional Customs Duty or Special CVD Protective Duty, Anti-dumping Duty Education Cess on Custom Duty
In International Economic Relations and International Politics, the most favoured nation (MFN) is a status or level of treatment accorded by one state to another in international trade.
The term means the country which is the recipient of this treatment must nominally receive equal trade advantages as the Most Favoured Nation by the country granting such treatment.
Most favoured nations for India are Bangladesh, Maldives, Nepal and Sri Lanka.

Advantages of most favoured nation These nations a get access to a wider market for better trade. They pay a lesser cost on their exports due to the reduction in trade barriers Due to the above opportunities, they get better options in terms of growth in business and competitiveness

Q. What is ODOP The One District One Product (ODOP) initiative aims to foster balanced regional development across all districts of India. Under this program, each district selects, brands, and promotes at least one product that represents its unique strengths.
Q. What is the goal of ODOP The goal is to enable holistic socioeconomic growth by leveraging local resources and creating employment opportunities
Q. Why are there two products listed against each district This is mainly done to accommodate one product each from Agriculture and engineering/manufacturing sectors.

Q. Whom should I reach out to avail benefits of this ODOP initiative You can contact district nodal officials of your respective district to understand more about this program and avail benefits of the program.

Q. For the promotion of my ODOP product, will I be given support to attend trade fairs or events Yes, please visit events and exhibition section of the website for more information about this or contact district nodal officials.

Q. How are Exports treated under GST All exports are deemed as inter-State supplies. Exports of goods and services are treated as zero rated supplies. The exporter has the option either to export under bond/Letter of Undertaking without payment of tax and claim refund of Input Tax Credit (ITC) or pay Integrated Goods and service tax (IGST) by utilizing ITC or in cash at the time of export and claim refund of IGST paid.

All exports are deemed as inter-State supplies. Exports of goods and services are treated as zero rated supplies. The exporter has the option either to export under bond/Letter of Undertaking without payment of tax and claim refund of Input Tax Credit (ITC) or pay Integrated Goods and service tax (IGST) by utilizing ITC or in cash at the time of export and claim refund of IGST paid.

B. Government of Maharashtras Maharashtra State Industrial Cluster Development Program (MSICDP)

Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) play a significant role in the economic development of the country. The sector contributes about 45% of the total production, 40% of the exports and about 69% of the employment opportunities. Considering the importance of MSME sector, the Central and the State Government have announced Industrial Cluster Development Programs based on the concept of collective development.
Industrial Cluster Development Program Minimum 20 nos. of working Micro/ Small units engaged in manufacturing of same/ similar products/ services under same category.

The Govt. of India is implementing the Micro, Small Enterprises-Cluster Development Program (MSE-CDP) since the year 2006, for the holistic development of the Micro and Small sector. The Government of Maharashtra has approved the States own scheme namely Maharashtra State Industrial Cluster Development Program (MSICDP) vide G.R. dated 25 February 2014, focusing on industrially backward areas for balanced growth of the State.

Under the Cluster Development Programs, the capacity building program namely Soft Intervention  physical common facility centre (CFC) namely Hard Intervention are being implemented with the help of financial support from Government of India  Government of Maharashtra.

The Common Facilities Center (CFC) includes, the facilities like Research and Development Center (RD), Packaging Center, Testing Facility, Training Center, Common Effluent Treatment Plant (CETP), Common Processing Center etc.

The Micro, Small Enterprises Cluster Development Program (MSE-CDP) is announced under the revised version by Govt. of India (GoI) on date 24 May 2022. Under revised guidelines, the Government of India gives financial support as Grant-In-Aid of 60%-80% of approved project cost (Considering the project cost of maximum of Rs. 30.00 Crore) to establish Common Facility Centre (CFC).

The scheme is being implemented in the State by the Directorate of Industries, a total of 54 projects are approved by Government of India for conducting interventions out of which a total of 47 projects got approval for setting up of CFC. As on date, 24 projects are operational, and rest are under construction stage.

The Government of Maharashtra vide G.R. dated 25 February 2014 announced the States own cluster development program namely Maharashtra State Industrial Cluster Development Program (MSICDP), focusing on Industrially backward areas viz. C, D, D, No Industry Districts  Naxalite Affected Areas.

Due to the effective implementation of cluster program, the concept of collective development is being accepted widely the confidence and trust building amongst the Micro  Small entrepreneurs has increased. The cluster intervention results in making SME sector more confident and competitive due to easy access of high-end technology. Around 25,000 SMEs in the State have benefitted which paves the way in creating substantial employment and self-employment opportunities in the State.
The scheme aims to create Critical Industrial Infrastructure which is directly relevant or helps to generate faster Industrial Development of the State.
Government of Maharashtra set up a Critical Infrastructure fund of Rs. 1,000 crs as part of Industrial Policy 2013.
68 proposals of 26 industrial estates have received grant since the launch providing benifit of Rs. 413 crs.
Government contributes 75% while the remaining 25% is contributed by stakeholders for development of critical infrastructure.

Entrepreneurial Development Training Programme
The main objects of the DIC programme are firstly to make available various assistance and clearance required under one roof and secondly to promote rural industries.

The objective of the scheme is to encourage unemployed person to take up self-employment ventures through industry, service and business, by providing soft loans to meet part of the margin money to avail institutional finance.
As per Govt. G.R. dated 18 May 2007, the Govt. of Maharashtra has made the following changes in the earlier Seed Money Scheme
The repayment of loan starts after three years in four yearly instalments. However, for vehicle cases repayment starts after six months of loan ailment.

In case of entrepreneur belonging to general category, the extent of Margin Money assistance is 20% of the total investment or ₹ 40,000/- whichever is less. Similarly in case of entrepreneurs belonging to scheduled caste  scheduled tribe Margin Money assistance of upto 30% of the total fixed capital investment or upto maximum of ₹ 60,000/- whichever is less is provided.

There is a provision of levying interest on this loan  of 4% p.a. and 1% penal interest in case of default in repayment schedule. Repayment of the margin money assistance is to be done within 4 years with an initial moratorium of six months. This scheme is particularly useful for rural artisans.
Following training programmes are organized-
o Entrepreneurship Introductory Programme (Udyojakata Parichay karyakram) of 1 day  Non-Residential

In this programme guidance and inputs on selection of activity, Entrepreneurship Personality Development, business management, information about various Government agencies and agencies providing financial assistance in the form of loan, etc. is imparted. Total expenses per programme are limited to ₹ 600/- per trainee.
o Entrepreneurship Development Training Programme (12 days Residential)

This programme comprises of 12 days residential training programme, which includes food expenses. Candidates identified and selected in Entrepreneurship Introductory Programme are given widespread information on Entrepreneurship Development. The institute imparting the training is given a grant of ₹ 4000/- per trainee.
o Technical Training Programme (15 days to 2 months Non-Residential)

This training programme comprise of information on latest and enhanced technical knowledge related to Production and Service. Trainees are given a stipend of ₹ 500/- after completion of the 15 days, ₹ 1000/- for 1 month and ₹ 2,000/- for 2 months of training programme. The training institute is given a grant of ₹ 3000/- per trainee.
Other initiatives and policies kindly refer the respective pages.
Projects cost increased from ₹ 10 lakhs to ₹ 25 lakhs for industry, service and business activity

Seed Money assistance at 15 per cent of the project cost approved by financial institutions is offered. In case of projects up to ₹ 10 lakhs, the quantum of assistance is 20% for SC/ST/OBC/NT/VT/Handicapped
Seed Money component up to ₹ 3.75 lakhs maximum

The rate of interest on seed money is 6% per annum and if the borrower repays instalment regularly and within schedule time, then the borrower will get rebate of 3% in interest. So he has to pay only 3% interest. Hence for regular repayment interest of 3% per annum
If the instalment is not repaid in time, it will attract 1% penal interest

Maharashtra is the second highest exporting state from India in FY 2023-24 with INR 5.56 lakh crore exports i.e., 15.37% of total exports from India. The top 5 exporting districts from the state are Mumbai Suburban, Mumbai City, Pune and Thane, contributing 74% of states total exports.
The top 10 importing countries form the State are USA, UAE, Hong Kong, Belgium, UK, China, Italy, Netherland, Germany, and Mexico.

All the districts in Maharashtra are exporting districts and have connectivity facilitated by air cargo terminals and Free Trade Zones. Top 5 Exporting Districts in FY 2023-24 with an exceptional growth compared to previous financial year FY 2022-23 are Amravati (108%), Chandrapur (93%), Washim (34%), Wardha (28%), and Sindhudurg (24%).

The major sectors contributing to the Maharashtras export are Gems  Jewellery (22.84%), Engineering (11.39%), Electronics and Electrical Components (17.30%), Chemicals (10.09%) and Pharmaceuticals (5.75%).

The state secured 2nd rank for the year 2022 in Export Preparedness Index (EPI) ranking published by NITI Aayog. Maharashtra is mapped as the leading state in India in the Export Ecosystem pillar and export infrastructure by the report.
The state of Maharashtra has the highest number of NABL-accredited Labs with 599 Labs and highest NABCB certification inspection agencies, with 55.
Maharashtra has held the highest number of trade fairs/exhibitions (110) and capacity building workshops (642) for its exporters which enable them to enter global markets.

MAITRI Empowering Maharashtras Investment Landscape

MAITRI is Maharashtras dedicated agency for driving economic growth, fostering innovation, and simplifying the investment process in the state. Established by the Government of Maharashtra, it plays a key role in making Maharashtra a preferred destination for investors.
Maharashtra offers world-class infrastructure, a skilled workforce, and access to a vast consumer market, making it an ideal state for business expansion and innovation.

Strategic Investment Facilitation MAITRI actively works to position Maharashtra as a top investment destination by offering investors a clear, efficient, and transparent process to set up and expand their businesses.
Collaborative Ecosystem Works closely with government bodies, industry associations, and investors to create a supportive environment for business growth.
Seamless Investment Process Provides investors with essential information, guides them through regulatory requirements, and accelerates approvals for timely project execution.
Focus on Sustainable Growth Prioritizes long-term value creation, fostering innovation, and ensuring the state remains competitive in key sectors like manufacturing, IT, infrastructure, and services.
Global Market Engagement Positions Maharashtra as a leader in global business by adapting to emerging market trends and offering businesses new opportunities for growth.
